questions.question: Which is NOT correct about the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court?

options.text: It can hear ordinary dispute of commercial nature between the Government of India and the states
It can hear any dispute between the Government of India and one or more states.
It can hear any dispute between the Government of India and any state or states on one side and one or more states on the other.
It can hear any dispute between two or more states.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** ​It can hear ordinary dispute of commercial nature between the Government of India and the states.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• There are three structures of jurisdiction for the Supreme Court:** Original, Appeal and Advisory.**
 
• A court has original jurisdiction if it is the **first court to hear a case.** 
 
• The SC has original jurisdiction in cases requiring foreign dignitaries, **one or more states, or cases requiring other public ministers.**
 
• The word original jurisdiction mentions to the question of which court has the authority to hear a **legal case for the first time.**

 The Supreme Court has original, appellate and advisory jurisdiction. 
 
• Its exclusive original jurisdiction extends to any dispute between the Government of India and one or more States or between the Government of India and any State or States on one side and one or more States on the other or between two or more States, if and insofar as the dispute involves any question (whether of law or fact) on which the existence or extent of a legal right depends. 
 
• In addition, Article 32 of the Constitution gives an extensive original jurisdiction to the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. 
 
• It is empowered to issue directions, orders or writs, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari to enforce them. 
 
• The Supreme Court has been conferred with power to direct transfer of any civil or criminal case from one High Court to another High Court or from a Court subordinate to another High Court.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the case of the Supreme Court in India, its original jurisdiction is** covered under Article 131. **
 
• Original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court** can hear any dispute between the Government of India and one or more states.**
 
• Original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court **can hear any dispute between the Government of India and any state or states on one side and one or more states on the other.**
 
• ​Original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court **can hear any dispute between two or more states**.

questions.question: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has introduced a PCA framework for large nonbanking financial companies (NBFCs) with effect from October 2022, putting restrictions whenever vital financial metrics dip below the prescribed threshold. What is PCA?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Prompt Corrective Action.**__ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Reserve Bank of India **has launched a** prompt corrective action** structure for large non-banking financial companies** (NBFCs).**
 
• **A prompt corrective action** structure,** launched for banks in 2002** and upgraded a couple of times after that, works as an** early warning signal for banks in stress.**
 
• The structure gets **activated when banks fail to meet certain financial limitations** that the regulator has sent as the minimum.
 
• **The central bank of India** is presently the only **Bank under PCA.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is the central bank of India, which started operations on **Apr. 1, 1935, under the Reserve Bank of India Act. **
 
• The Reserve Bank of India uses financial policy to generate **financial firmness in India**, and it is charged with regulating the country's currency and credit systems.​
 
• It controls the **monetary policy regarding the national currency**, the Indian rupee.

questions.question: Which is NOT correct about the Directive Principles of the State Policy?

options.text: They are mentioned in Part IV of the Constitution of India.
They aim to establish a welfare state in India.
They are a novel feature of the Constitution of India.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They are justiciable in nature.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy** motive to generate** social and economic** conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life. 
 
• They as well motive to start **social and economic democracy** through a welfare state.
 
• The main aim of the Directive Principle of State Policy **listed in Part 4 of the Indian Constitution** is to give economic justice and to avoid the** concentration of wealth in the hands of a few people**.
 
• So, no government **can afford to ignore them.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Directive Principles** together with the Fundamental Rights hold the** philosophy of the Constitution and are the soul of the Constitution.**
 
• **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** reported these principles as** 'novel features' **of the Indian Constitution.​ 
 
• **Part IV of the Constitution of India (Article 36–51)** holds the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).

questions.question: Deficiency of which vitamin causes symptoms like tingling in the tongue, anaemia, white patches on the skin, mouth ulcers and shortness of breath?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin B12.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vitamin deficiency anemia** is a situation that develops when you have low levels of** vitamin B12**.
 
• In this kind of anemia, human body doesn't generate **enough healthy red blood cells. **
 
• Having low levels of **vitamin B-12** can make human tongue sore and swollen and affect humans** sense of taste.**
 
• Anemia that reactions from **vitamin B-12 deficiency **may cause a person to feel a little short of breath. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vitamin E deficiency** can cause a form of anemia in which red blood cells rupture.
 
• **Vitamin K deficiency** bleeding, happens when babies cannot control bleeding as their blood does not have **sufficient Vitamin K to form a clot**. ​ 
 
• A **deficiency of vitamin B1** generally leads to beriberi, a situation that features **problems with the peripheral nerves and wasting.**
